The output also reads csc_escalation.10379 (the state:46 unit, grandchild exit) with weight -0.005. 30 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, 4000 rows, local in-memory forward passes): full AUC 0.9193; all nonlinear children replaced by least-squares linear fits on their entries 0.8303 (jointly 0.8297; refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433). Shapley split of the gain: gate 0.041, day-charge 0.023, heavy-usage 0.022. Removing all state effects drops AUC to 0.9094 (0.010). parts.name: service_call_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Many customer-service calls AND low usage -> churn. 997 = relu(0.389*CSC + 0.494*csc_escalation.7689 - 1.718*usage_brake.4397 + 0.206*usage_brake.1694_b - 0.641), readout +3.108. The convex service-call signal pushes 997 up; the usage ramp 4397 shuts it for anyone with average or higher day usage. Mean contribution: 0 for 0-2 calls at any usage; at 3 calls +1.25 logit below 150 day minutes, +0.6 at 150-180; at 4 calls +4.0 / +2.6 / +0.9 (below 150 / 150-180 / 180-200 minutes); at 5 calls +7.0 / +4.4 / +2.6; at 6+ calls +10.7 / +8.5 / +5.5; about 0 above 220 minutes except for 6+ calls. Train churn with 4+ calls and under 150 day minutes is 87-100% (86 rows) vs 4-6% for 0-3 calls.
